public_body: Pioneer Valley Performing Arts Charter School Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving and then revising insufficiently detailed minutes of its March 11 meeting, omitting summaries of public comments; intent was not found and other allegations were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Original minutes of the March 11 meeting gave public comment duration and speaker time but no summary of what the fourteen speakers said.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board created insufficiently detailed minutes by failing to include any summary of the statements, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Revised minutes still omitted the subject matter of two letters that speakers read aloud during public comment, so they were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board’s revised minutes are insufficiently detailed as they fail to include summaries of these two public comments, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant later alleged the revised minutes violated speakers' privacy by naming them; this was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review these allegations, as our review is limited to the allegations of violations of the Open Meeting Law that were clearly and sufficiently raised in the original complaint filed with the public body.

allegations.summary: Complainant later alleged the Board improperly accepted revised minutes without a vote; this was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Although we decline to review the additional allegations, we note that the Open Meeting Law does not govern the method for approving meeting minutes or the handling of private information in open session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the minutes violation was intentional; the AG considered whether the violation was knowing under G.L. c. 30A § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: We have not previously warned the Board against the violation found here, nor do we find other evidence that would support a finding of an intentional violation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within thirty days of receipt of the letter, amend the March 11 minutes to include a summary of the public comments made by the two speakers who read from submitted letters.
remedy_passage: we order the Board, within thirty days of receipt of this letter, to amend the minutes of the March 11 meeting to include a summary of the public comments made by the two speakers who read from letters they submitted to the Board.
